1	# Memory Architecture
2	
3	Two parallel systems handle persistence across Pi sessions. They serve different roles and complement each other.
4	
5	**Full internals comparison:** [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) — source-backed deep dive vs Claude Code + Codex.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Systems at a glance
10	
11	| | dream-memory | pi-memory |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **Role** | Read path — inject context at session start; owns 24h/N-session consolidation (CC `autoDream`) | Write path — per-turn memory extraction (CC `extractMemories`) |
14	| **Storage root** | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
15	| **Trigger** | `dispatchSessionStart` (once per session, turn 1) | `turn_end` hook, per-turn (throttle `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS`, default 1); no time/session gate |
16	| **Injection point** | Stable `<persistent-memory>` snapshot (turn 1 only; cache-safe) | Per-turn fork (`maxTurns: 5`) + shutdown flush; active recall appends at the message tail when enabled |
17	| **Source extension** | `my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/` | `my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/` |
18	| **Key entrypoint** | `src/harness-cli.ts` | `index.ts` |
19	| **Subagent** | None (file read only) | `general` (forked, bounded toolset) |
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Merge status (2026-06-02)
24	
25	dream→pi-memory consolidation in progress. Current reality:
26	
27	- **dream-memory is `retired`** — in no profile manifest (`my-pi-full` loads only `pi-memory`); `harness-cli.ts` is dead code. Kept for migration reference.
28	- **Profile injection moved into pi-memory** (read-path responsibility): the `pi-memory.profile-base` `systemPrompt:build` filter (priority 10) injects a byte-stable snapshot rendered from the curated obsidian profile files (`00-pi-active-context.md` + `MEMORY.md`) into the cacheable base. `cache-base-prompt` (priority 90, `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`) relocates it cross-cwd. Snapshot file: `~/.pi/agent/dream-memory/profile-memory.md`; refreshed on `session_start` when stale (tracks the hourly autoDream run). See `extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`.
29	- **Obsidian-tree consolidation still runs** via the `dream-consolidation` routine (`pnpm dream pending`, watched by `com.pi-routine.watch-dream-consolidation`, gated to ~hourly). Its prompt already mirrors the instruction-refiner + progressive-disclosure discipline (`dream/dream.ts:654`). pi-tree extraction (per-turn) is unchanged.
30	- **Recall UX** (pi-memory): hits deliver as a single collapsible thinking-styled custom message (`pi_memory_recall`) on the next turn, past the cache breakpoint — not a user-text transform; slim footer `🧠 N · Xms`. See `src/recall-message.ts`.
31	- **qmd inline recall is ON (resolved 2026-06-02, qmd 2.5.3).** The 2.5.1 SIGABRT-on-teardown was an upstream darwin-Metal bug: the `ggml_metal_device` destructor asserts `[rsets->data count] == 0` during `__cxa_finalize_ranges`, only firing when `process.exit()` skips Node's `beforeExit` (which node-llama-cpp uses to dispose Metal contexts). Fixed upstream in tobi/qmd 2.5.3 (`finishSuccessfulCliCommand` sets `process.exitCode = 0` and returns instead of calling `process.exit(0)`). No local patch needed — bumped the global binary `@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.1→2.5.3 (`npm i -g @tobilu/qmd@latest`). After the upgrade, `qmd query` exits 0 and federated multi-collection recall returns correct hits (the earlier `vsearch` 0-hits was 2.1-era flakiness; resolved post-embed-repair). Recall path is now the **structured reranked `qmd query`** (`vec:`+`lex:` lines supplied by us → skips the ~20 s LLM HyDE auto-expansion but keeps the reranker; `qmd search` drops rerank, `qmd vsearch` is vector-only), federated via repeated `-c` across `pi-memory` + `dream-memory-{profile,project,tools}`. Warm latency ~1.0–1.3 s (timeout ceiling 3000 ms); a cold MLX embedder/reranker reload after idle can spike to ~16 s for a novel query, so on a cold miss the recall **gracefully falls back to the in-process lexical scan** (no crash, no hang) and steady-state turns get federated reranked qmd hits. The merge respects `route`: when `route:"qmd"` returns hits they ARE the result (qmd's 0–1 rerank scores are otherwise buried under the lexical term-frequency counts); lexical is the fallback only when qmd is empty. Recall still blocks the turn so hits land in-turn (quality over latency, per Luke; `extensions/pi-memory/index.ts` input handler). Config: `recall.route:"qmd"`, `recall.qmd.enabled:true`, `recall.qmd.collections:[…]` in `config/defaults.json` + `src/config.ts`; wiring in `src/qmd.ts:searchQmdCli`. The warm-REST alternative (`searchQmdHttp`) federates the same collections if a `qmd serve` listener is ever enabled (`httpPort`).
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Injection ownership + A/B deadline (2026-06-10)
36	
37	Oracle-reviewed disposition (`docs/pi-harness-optimisation/2026-06-08/findings/oracle-tokenjuice-dream-memory-verdict.md`, gpt-5.5-pro):
38	
39	- **pi-memory owns model-facing profile memory injection.** It is the only extension allowed to inject profile context into the cached base (`extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`).
40	- **dream-memory stays out of the Pi profile.** Allowed roles if revived: shutdown consolidation, event-log processing, obsidian wiki maintenance, offline A/B, cross-harness export. Not allowed: SessionStart/base/project/recall injection or extra memory tools. Any re-add first requires a tested **single-owner injection guard** covering base blocks, `<persistent-memory>`, and model-facing recall.
41	- **letta-shadow + mem0-shadow stay true shadows**: observe/write/compare only — no model-facing injection, no variable tools, no dynamic context before the cache boundary.
42	
43	**A/B deadline — by 2026-06-30 or after 30 representative sessions** (oracle-recommended default, adopted 2026-06-10; Luke can override): choose the primary memory path, keep shadows only with measurable lift, retire dream-memory Pi injection unless it wins a defined metric. Metrics: cache-base churn, recall precision, recall usefulness (did it change the next action?), user-correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool-call overhead, prompt bytes per session, wrong-action vs rework-prevented counts.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## dream-memory — read path
48	
49	Injects a deterministic subset of `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` on the **first turn of every session**. This is a cache-stable snapshot, not a live recall feed.
50	
51	Hard caps: **24 kB total / 8 files**. YAML frontmatter is stripped before injection so event ids, dream timestamps, and other provenance fields do not change the cached prompt prefix.
52	
53	**Loader order** (lex-sorted within each root, stops at cap):
54	
55	1. `profile/` — durable cross-project preferences, identity, tooling config
56	2. `project/<slug>/` — only when cwd resolves to that slug (via `.dream-memory.yml` or git remote)
57	3. repowise summary (`.repowise/` index, if present in repo)
58	
59	**Not injected into the cached prefix** (but indexed; accessible via active recall or dream consolidation):
60	- `inbox/` — raw uncurated notes
61	- `archive/` — session logs, RCAs, one-off notes
62	- `tools/`, `memory-archive-*/`
63	
64	**Anchor file:** `profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — loads first (lex-sort), ≤1500 tok briefing card. Keep it **cache-stable**: no dates, no session counters, no event ids.
65	
66	**Config:** `DREAM_WIKI_HOME=~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`
67	
68	---
69	
70	## pi-memory — write path
71	
72	Consolidates session learning into structured memory files. Uses Claude Code's `memdir/` storage shape (same type taxonomy, filename convention, frontmatter shape, MEMORY.md index pattern), but Pi keeps the main-session prompt compact: the parent sees memory availability, safety, and minimal inline-write guidance; the full write protocol lives in the extractor prompt and `pi-memory-save` skill.
73	
74	**On-disk layout:**
75	
76	```
77	~/.pi/agent/memory/
78	├── profile/
79	│   ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (cross-project memories)
80	│   ├── user_*.md
81	│   └── feedback_*.md
82	└── project/<slug>/
83	    ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (project-specific memories)
84	    ├── project_*.md
85	    └── reference_*.md
86	```
87	
88	**Type taxonomy:** `user | feedback | project | reference`
89	
90	**Trigger gates (v3, 2026-05-16):**
91	
92	| Gate | Default | Env override |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| Time since last consolidation | 24 h | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS` |
95	| Sessions since last consolidation | 5 | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS` |
96	| Re-scan throttle | 10 min | `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS` |
97	| Cross-process lock | per-scope `.consolidate-lock-<scope>` mtime file | — |
98	| Pollution skip | sessions with `web_search`, `mcp_*`, `WebFetch` | `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_OVERRIDES_PRIORITY=1` |
99	
100	**Prompt templates:** `extensions/pi-memory/prompts/`
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Active-recall — the bridge between the two
105	
106	`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory.ts` provides the experimental **per-turn read side** for both stores. It can rank `qmd` vector-index hits across federated collections and inject relevant memories as a custom message. Delivery is cache-safe only when the Pi extension filters stale active-recall messages out of the transcript view and appends the current settled recall at the tail of the next model call.
107	
108	**Collections in default recall:**
109	
110	| Collection | Backs |
111	|---|---|
112	| `pi-memory` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
113	| `dream-memory-profile` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` |
114	| `dream-memory-project` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/` |
115	| `scars` | scar-tissue patterns |
116	| `changes` | notable change log entries |
117	
118	**Enable:** set `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1` for an explicit live opt-in, or edit `~/.dream-memory/recall.toml` to `enabled = true`. `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=0` remains a kill switch.
119	
120	**Circuit breaker:** fires only if `candidate_limit` (40) hits pass a relevance threshold (`auto_none_threshold` 0.4). Never fires inside pi-memory subagents (`isPiMemorySubAgent` guard).
121	
122	---
123	
124	## Adding memories manually
125	
126	| What | Where |
127	|---|---|
128	| Durable cross-project preference | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/<topic>.md` |
129	| Project-specific fact | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/<slug>/<topic>.md` |
130	| Quick inbox note | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/inbox/<name>.md` (vector-indexed only; not injected) |
131	| Session learning (auto) | pi-memory writes to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` after the session |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Diagnosing bloat
136	
137	```bash
138	pi-cache-stats --all   # watch turn-1 `write` column
139	```
140	
141	A clean baseline from `~/Projects/personal/<repo>` sits at ≤ ~35 kB write on turn 1. If it jumps:
142	
143	1. Audit `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` — keep total ≤ 3 kB
144	2. Check `project/<slug>/` for large files; move bulk content to `archive/`
145	3. Verify `inbox/` is draining through dream; it should be indexed/searchable, not first-turn injected
146	
147	---
148

151	| Doc | When to read |
152	|---|---|
153	| [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) | Source-backed deep dive; CC + Codex comparison; v3 gap analysis |
154	| [`global-memory-architecture.md`](./global-memory-architecture.md) | Source/profile/role/cache/sync design for future cross-runtime memory |
155	| [`global-memory-eval-corpus.md`](./global-memory-eval-corpus.md) | Retrieval-quality, permission-leak, stale/contradiction eval fixtures |

- **qmd inline recall is ON (resolved 2026-06-02, qmd 2.5.3).** The 2.5.1 SIGABRT-on-teardown was an upstream darwin-Metal bug: the `ggml_metal_device` destructor asserts `[rsets->data count] == 0` during `__cxa_finalize_ranges`, only firing when `process.exit()` skips Node's `beforeExit` (which node-llama-cpp uses to dispose Metal contexts). Fixed upstream in tobi/qmd 2.5.3 (`finishSuccessfulCliCommand` sets `process.exitCode = 0` and returns instead of calling `process.exit(0)`). No local patch needed — bumped the global binary `@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.1→2.5.3 (`npm i -g @tobilu/qmd@latest`). After the upgrade, `qmd query` exits 0 and federated multi-collection recall returns correct hits (the earlier `vsearch` 0-hits was 2.1-era flakiness; resolved post-embed-repair). Recall path is now the **structured reranked `qmd query`** (`vec:`+`lex:` lines supplied by us → skips the ~20 s LLM HyDE auto-expansion but keeps the reranker; `qmd search` drops rerank, `qmd vsearch` is vector-only), federated via repeated `-c` across `pi-memory` + `dream-memory-{profile,project,tools}`. Warm latency ~1.0–1.3 s (timeout ceiling 3000 ms); a cold MLX embedder/reranker reload after idle can spike to ~16 s for a novel query, so on a cold miss the recall **gracefully falls back to the in-process lexical scan** (no crash, no hang) and steady-state turns get federated reranked qmd hits. The merge respects `route`: when `route:"qmd"` returns hits they ARE the result (qmd's 0–1 rerank scores are otherwise buried under the lexical term-frequency counts); lexical is the fallback only when qmd is empty. Recall still blocks the turn so hits land in-turn (quality over latency, per Luke; `extensions/pi-memory/index.ts` input handler). Config: `recall.route:"qmd"`, `recall.qmd.enabled:true`, `recall.qmd.collections:[…]` in `config/defaults.json` + `src/config.ts`; wiring in `src/qmd.ts:searchQmdCli`. The warm-REST alternative (`searchQmdHttp`) federates the same collections if a `qmd serve` listener is ever enabled (`httpPort`).

---

## Injection ownership + A/B deadline (2026-06-10)

Oracle-reviewed disposition (`docs/pi-harness-optimisation/2026-06-08/findings/oracle-tokenjuice-dream-memory-verdict.md`, gpt-5.5-pro):

- **pi-memory owns model-facing profile memory injection.** It is the only extension allowed to inject profile context into the cached base (`extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`).
- **dream-memory stays out of the Pi profile.** Allowed roles if revived: shutdown consolidation, event-log processing, obsidian wiki maintenance, offline A/B, cross-harness export. Not allowed: SessionStart/base/project/recall injection or extra memory tools. Any re-add first requires a tested **single-owner injection guard** covering base blocks, `<persistent-memory>`, and model-facing recall.
- **letta-shadow + mem0-shadow stay true shadows**: observe/write/compare only — no model-facing injection, no variable tools, no dynamic context before the cache boundary.

**A/B deadline — by 2026-06-30 or after 30 representative sessions** (oracle-recommended default, adopted 2026-06-10; Luke can override): choose the primary memory path, keep shadows only with measurable lift, retire dream-memory Pi injection unless it wins a defined metric. Metrics: cache-base churn, recall precision, recall usefulness (did it change the next action?), user-correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool-call overhead, prompt bytes per session, wrong-action vs rework-prevented counts.

---

## dream-memory — read path

Injects a deterministic subset of `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` on the **first turn of every session**. This is a cache-stable snapshot, not a live recall feed.

Hard caps: **24 kB total / 8 files**. YAML frontmatter is stripped before injection so event ids, dream timestamps, and other provenance fields do not change the cached prompt prefix.

**Loader order** (lex-sorted within each root, stops at cap):

1. `profile/` — durable cross-project preferences, identity, tooling config
2. `project/<slug>/` — only when cwd resolves to that slug (via `.dream-memory.yml` or git remote)
3. repowise summary (`.repowise/` index, if present in repo)

**Not injected into the cached prefix** (but indexed; accessible via active recall or dream consolidation):
- `inbox/` — raw uncurated notes
- `archive/` — session logs, RCAs, one-off notes
- `tools/`, `memory-archive-*/`

**Anchor file:** `profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — loads first (lex-sort), ≤1500 tok briefing card. Keep it **cache-stable**: no dates, no session counters, no event ids.

**Config:** `DREAM_WIKI_HOME=~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`

---

## pi-memory — write path

Consolidates session learning into structured memory files. Uses Claude Code's `memdir/` storage shape (same type taxonomy, filename convention, frontmatter shape, MEMORY.md index pattern), but Pi keeps the main-session prompt compact: the parent sees memory availability, safety, and minimal inline-write guidance; the full write protocol lives in the extractor prompt and `pi-memory-save` skill.

**On-disk layout:**

```
~/.pi/agent/memory/
├── profile/
│   ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (cross-project memories)
│   ├── user_*.md
│   └── feedback_*.md
└── project/<slug>/
    ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (project-specific memories)
    ├── project_*.md
    └── reference_*.md
```

**Type taxonomy:** `user | feedback | project | reference`

**Trigger gates (v3, 2026-05-16):**

| Gate | Default | Env override |
|---|---|---|
| Time since last consolidation | 24 h | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS` |
| Sessions since last consolidation | 5 | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS` |
| Re-scan throttle | 10 min | `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS` |
| Cross-process lock | per-scope `.consolidate-lock-<scope>` mtime file | — |
| Pollution skip | sessions with `web_search`, `mcp_*`, `WebFetch` | `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_OVERRIDES_PRIORITY=1` |

**Prompt templates:** `extensions/pi-memory/prompts/`

---

## Active-recall — the bridge between the two

`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory.ts` provides the experimental **per-turn read side** for both stores. It can rank `qmd` vector-index hits across federated collections and inject relevant memories as a custom message. Delivery is cache-safe only when the Pi extension filters stale active-recall messages out of the transcript view and appends the current settled recall at the tail of the next model call.

**Collections in default recall:**

| Collection | Backs |
|---|---|
| `pi-memory` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
| `dream-memory-profile` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` |
| `dream-memory-project` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/` |
| `scars` | scar-tissue patterns |
| `changes` | notable change log entries |

**Enable:** set `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1` for an explicit live opt-in, or edit `~/.dream-memory/recall.toml` to `enabled = true`. `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=0` remains a kill switch.

**Circuit breaker:** fires only if `candidate_limit` (40) hits pass a relevance threshold (`auto_none_threshold` 0.4). Never fires inside pi-memory subagents (`isPiMemorySubAgent` guard).

---

## Adding memories manually

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Durable cross-project preference | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/<topic>.md` |
| Project-specific fact | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/<slug>/<topic>.md` |
| Quick inbox note | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/inbox/<name>.md` (vector-indexed only; not injected) |
| Session learning (auto) | pi-memory writes to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` after the session |

---

## Diagnosing bloat

```bash
pi-cache-stats --all   # watch turn-1 `write` column
```

A clean baseline from `~/Projects/personal/<repo>` sits at ≤ ~35 kB write on turn 1. If it jumps:

1. Audit `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` — keep total ≤ 3 kB
2. Check `project/<slug>/` for large files; move bulk content to `archive/`
3. Verify `inbox/` is draining through dream; it should be indexed/searchable, not first-turn injected

---

## Related docs

| Doc | When to read |
|---|---|
| [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) | Source-backed deep dive; CC + Codex comparison; v3 gap analysis |
| [`global-memory-architecture.md`](./global-memory-architecture.md) | Source/profile/role/cache/sync design for future cross-runtime memory |
| [`global-memory-eval-corpus.md`](./global-memory-eval-corpus.md) | Retrieval-quality, permission-leak, stale/contradiction eval fixtures |
| [`memory-query-prototype.md`](./memory-query-prototype.md) | Local read-only deferred `memory_query` prototype boundary |
| [`cache-strategy.md`](./cache-strategy.md) | How memory extraction avoids cache breaks in forked agents |
| `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md` | Mandatory checklist when touching fork/extension memory code |

content.text: Now the cross-harness parity docs — these are exactly the question being asked.

content.content:
1	# Goal: Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)
2	
3	**Purpose.** Make Claude Code CLI, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, and the Codex app carry — as far as each architecturally *can* — the same **skills, tools, and functionality** Luke has built in `my-pi` + `pi-mono-fork`, then **measure** parity with one command, **confirm** it with evidence, and **maintain** it with an automated drift gate + propagation pipeline.
4	
5	**How to use this doc.**
6	- §A is the copy-paste **goal prompt**.
7	- §B–§I are the spec: the parity model, success definition, acceptance, measurement, architecture, phases, non-negotiables, risks.
8	- §J is the **baseline scorecard** captured 2026-06-22 (real numbers — re-run the scanner to refresh).
9	- Appendix = grounded tool/path reference so the executing agent doesn't hallucinate the tooling.
10	
11	**Status (2026-06-22) — GET-parity achieved across the harnesses Luke uses; goal closeable.** T1 skill parity is **closed**: Codex and Pi at **100%** canonical coverage, Claude Code at **104/105** with one reasoned exclusion (`context`, Codex-native — see §J); the gate (`npm run parity:gate`) was proven failing before propagation (exit 1) and passing after (exit 0), and re-proven catching live drift when a new SoT skill (`context`) landed unpropagated (exit 1 → classify → exit 0). The scanner (`scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`), the CI-safe gate (wired into `gate:ci`), the generated drift report (`docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md`), and the T3 equivalence map (`docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`) all exist.
12	
13	**The Desktop reframing (resolves T2).** "Claude Desktop" is **two surfaces**, not one (see §0): (a) **native chat** — no skills dir, MCP-only — and (b) **Claude Code running inside the desktop app** — shares `~/.claude/` config + `~/.claude/skills`, already T1-covered. **Luke uses (b), not (a).** The CHP MCP server's *only unique* consumer was (a) native chat — the one surface with no other way to reach skills. Since Luke doesn't use it, T2 **live-wiring is descoped**: every harness in Luke's actual loop (Claude Code in terminal **and** desktop app, Codex CLI/app, Pi) already carries the skills via T1. The CHP MCP server (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) stays **built + deployed + tested** on the shelf (verified over the real MCP stdio protocol, deployed to `~/.local/share/chp/`); the runbook `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` flips it live in ~60s **if** Luke ever adopts native chat or wants a genuinely portable Pi tool bridged. `PARITY.requiredMcp` stays empty so the gate remains green/honest — T2 mechanism *proven*, not switched on by choice.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## §0 — The reframing that makes this tractable
18	
19	"Parity" is **not one thing**. Luke's Pi surface splits into three portability tiers, and the honest goal differs per tier. Forcing tier-3 into tier-1 is how this turns into an infinite project.
20	
21	| Tier | What it is | Parity means | Target harnesses |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **T1 — Portable** | Skills (markdown `SKILL.md` + `references/`) | The *same skill files* present & loadable | CC, Codex, Pi (all support a skills dir). **Desktop cannot** — no skills dir. |
24	| **T2 — Adaptable** | Pi tools that are really CLI/HTTP under a thin Pi wrapper: `fuse`, `advisor`, `semantic_grep`, `task-tools`, tokenjuice, OTel | An **equivalent MCP server or CLI** exposed to the harness | CC, Codex, Desktop (MCP is the universal seam) |
25	| **T3 — Pi-native** | Runtime behavior fused to Pi/claude-bridge: cache-base-prompt boundary, memory-v3 injection, fork-mode sibling cache, deferred-tool coordination, `setActiveTools` guard, goal state machine, worktree mutation blocker | A **documented native equivalent** (e.g. Codex has native memories/goals; CC has hooks) **or an accepted N/A** — never a port | per-harness; mostly N/A |
26	
27	The whole project hangs on this: **drive T1 to ~100% mechanically, expose the worthwhile T2 tools via MCP once and wire everywhere, and for T3 maintain a documented equivalence map — don't chase ports that can't exist.** The hard architectural fact: **Claude Desktop's native chat has only one extensibility surface — MCP servers** — so *that surface's* parity is bounded to T2 + whatever skills we serve *through* an MCP "skills" server.
28	
29	**Critical scoping fact (2026-06-22):** "Claude Desktop" is **two distinct surfaces**, and they have opposite parity stories:
30	- **Desktop native chat** — no skills dir, MCP-only. The *only* harness whose skills must arrive via the T2 MCP bridge. **Luke does not use this surface.**
31	- **Claude Code inside the desktop app** — same `~/.claude/settings.json` + `~/.claude/skills` as the CLI; loads skills natively (T1). **This is Luke's actual desktop usage**, and it's already covered.
32	
33	Consequence: the CHP MCP server's *unique* value (skills-into-a-skill-less harness) targets a surface Luke doesn't run. So T2 is built and proven but **live-wiring is descoped** — every harness Luke touches already has the skills via T1. Wiring stays a 60-second runbook step for the day that changes.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## §A — The Goal Prompt (paste this)
38	
39	> Build the **Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)** system described in `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md`. Work phase by phase (§F); each phase ships a deliverable **and** its verification before the next starts. Do not claim a phase done without the evidence named in its "Verify" line.
40	>
41	> The system must let me, with one command: (1) **measure** parity — a read-only scanner emits a scorecard of skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents coverage per harness (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Pi) against the canonical source of truth, classifying each capability into the §0 tiers; (2) **confirm** parity — a CI gate (`check:harness-parity`) fails when a harness drifts below its declared tier target, with the drift rendered to a committed report; (3) **close gaps** — drive T1 (skills) to ~100% via an idempotent propagation pipeline with per-agent targeting, expose chosen T2 tools as a single MCP server wired into every harness, and record T3 capabilities in an equivalence map (native-equivalent / accepted-N/A); (4) **maintain** it — the gate runs in `gate:ci` and a `weekly-review` cadence catches drift as skills/tools are added.
42	>
43	> Honor the §G non-negotiables (measure before claiming, read-only scanner with no model/API calls, three-tier honesty — no T3 ports, MCP-once-wire-everywhere for T2, single source of truth for skills, every recurring action is a script wrapper). Reuse existing tooling — extend `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (the static catalog scanner) and its `registry.generated.json` schema, the `drift.generated.md` output surface, `scripts/skills` (symlink propagation), the `prototypes/skill-sync` engine, and `gate:ci`. Only the new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the MCP exposure of T2 tools, and the propagation `--agent` targeting. When all phases are green, write the runbook (§F Phase 5) and report the final scorecard.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## §B — Definition of success
48	
49	Success = Luke can run a **repeatable, evidence-backed loop** that:
50	
51	1. **Measures** parity per harness in one command, tier-classified, against the canonical SoT.
52	2. **Confirms** parity in CI — a gate fails on drift below each harness's declared tier target, drift rendered to a committed report.
53	3. **Closes** the gaps: T1 skills at the agreed coverage on every skills-capable harness; the chosen T2 tools reachable as MCP in CC, Codex, and Desktop; T3 capabilities each marked native-equivalent or accepted-N/A in a committed map.
54	4. **Maintains** itself: adding a skill or tool to the SoT and re-running propagation + scan brings every harness back to target with **no manual symlinking**, and the gate catches anyone who forgets.
55	
56	"Done" is not "configs touched." Done is: the §C checklist is green with the §D evidence committed, and the §H drill passes.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## §C — Acceptance checklist (every item needs evidence)
61	
62	| # | Requirement | Evidence |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| C1 | Parity scanner exists, read-only | `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` runs from a clean worktree, makes no model/API calls, mutates nothing; emits the §D scorecard schema |
65	| C2 | Tier classification | Every measured capability tagged T1/T2/T3; the T3 equivalence map (`docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`) lists each Pi-native capability × harness as native-equiv / accepted-N/A |
66	| C3 | Scanner covers 4 harnesses | Scorecard has rows for Pi, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex with skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents surfaces; Desktop correctly shows skills=N/A, MCP-only |
67	| C4 | Drift gate | `npm run check:harness-parity` exits non-zero when any harness is below its declared target; passes when at/above; drift rendered to `docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md` |
68	| C5 | T1 skill parity closed | Skills-capable harnesses (CC, Codex, Pi) at the agreed coverage of the canonical SoT (target ≥99%, justified exclusions listed); zero dangling symlinks |
69	| C6 | Propagation pipeline | One idempotent command syncs the SoT to a chosen `--agent` (claude-code/codex/pi/all); re-running is a no-op; a `status`/`diff` subcommand reports per-harness missing/extra/dangling |
70	| C7 | T2 tools exposed | ≥1 chosen adaptable Pi tool (e.g. `fuse` or `advisor`) packaged as an MCP server and wired into CC (`mcpServers`), Codex (`[mcp_servers]`), and Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`); the scanner counts it present in all three |
71	| C8 | New-capability drill | Adding one skill to the SoT and one tool to the MCP server, then re-running propagation + scan, brings all harnesses to target with **zero manual edits** (demonstrated in §H) |
72	| C9 | Maintenance wiring | `parity:gate` is in `gate:ci`; the cadence + full command-map runbook live in `docs/pi-setup/harness-parity-maintenance.md` (measure / confirm / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard) |
73	| C10 | Auditability | The scorecard is committed per run under `docs/pi-setup/generated/`; `git log` reconstructs parity over time |
74	
75	---
76	
77	## §D — How parity is measured (no vibes)
78	
79	**The scorecard contract** (`harness-parity-scan.mjs --json`, `schemaVersion: 1`): per harness, per surface (`skills`, `mcp`, `hooks`, `commands`, `agents`, `features`):
80	- `supported: bool` — does the harness *architecturally* carry this surface? (Desktop skills → `false`.)
81	- For skills: `{total, canonicalCovered, canonicalTotal, parityPct, missing[], extra[], dangling[]}` vs the canonical SoT.
82	- For MCP/hooks/commands/agents: configured names + counts.
83	
84	**Parity targets** (declared per harness, gate-enforced in C4):
85	- **T1 skills** — CC / Codex / Pi: `parityPct ≥ 99` of the canonical set minus a committed exclusion list (worktree-local, harness-specific, or package-declared skills). `dangling == 0` always.
86	- **T2 MCP** — the chosen CHP MCP server present in CC, Codex, Desktop.
87	- **T3** — presence in the equivalence map, not a numeric threshold.
88	
89	**Drift gate** (`check:harness-parity`, exit≠0 ⇒ red): any skills-capable harness below its T1 target, any dangling symlink, or the CHP MCP server missing from a T2 target. Rendered to `harness-parity.generated.md`.
90	
91	**Honest exclusions, never silent.** A skill legitimately absent from a harness (e.g. a Pi-only orchestration skill on Codex) goes in the committed exclusion list with a one-line reason. "Missing and unexplained" fails the gate; "missing and listed" passes. No silent truncation of coverage.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## §E — Architecture (grounded in existing tools)
96	
97	Four components. **Reuse first** — the only new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and propagation `--agent` targeting.
98	
99	**A. Parity scanner** — *new glue, extends the catalog model.* `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` (shipped, v0). Reads canonical SoT + each harness's skills dir and config (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` + `hooks.json`, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`). Emits the §D scorecard. Next: fold its observations into `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs`'s `registry.generated.json` (add a `buildHarnessSnapshot()` beside `buildSnapshot()`) so parity lives in the same CMDB as the Pi catalog, and render `harness-parity.generated.md` (today a placeholder lives at `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`).
100	
101	**B. T1 propagation** — *extend `scripts/skills` + `prototypes/skill-sync`.* Today `scripts/skills link --apply` symlinks the whole SoT into all three harness roots; it has no `--agent` filter and no `status`/`diff`. Add: per-agent targeting (`--agent claude-code|codex|pi|all`), a `status`/`diff` subcommand (the read side the scanner already computes), and dangling-link repair. The tested `prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` diff-cache engine is the basis for the eventual `npx skills` CLI that syncs **remote** runtimes (Mac Mini, pods) — local stays symlinks.
102	
103	**C. T2 MCP exposure** — *new, small.* Package the worthwhile adaptable tools (start with one: `fuse` or `advisor`) as a single **CHP MCP server** (stdio). Wire it into all three MCP-capable harnesses' configs. One server, wired everywhere = the cheapest path to tool parity *and* the only path that reaches Desktop. Pi keeps using its native extension; the MCP server wraps the same underlying CLI/logic so behavior matches.
104	
105	**D. T3 equivalence map** — *docs, not code.* `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`: a table of each Pi-native capability × harness → `native-equivalent: <what>` / `accepted-N/A: <why>`. This is the parity *contract* for the un-portable tier; the scanner links to it so "not measured here" is explicit, not a gap.
106	
107	**E. Maintenance** — *extend `gate:ci` + `weekly-review`.* Add `check:harness-parity` to the `gate:ci` chain; document the weekly cadence in the `weekly-review` skill. Adding a skill/tool to the SoT → propagation + scan → gate stays green.
108	
109	```
110	  canonical SoT (~/Projects/personal/skills) ──┐
111	                                                ▼
112	   (B) propagation ──► CC / Codex / Pi skills dirs ──┐
113	   (C) CHP MCP server ─► CC / Codex / Desktop mcp ──► (A) scanner ──► scorecard + drift report
114	   (D) T3 equivalence map ────────────────────────────┘                    │
115	                                                                            ▼
116	                                                            (E) check:harness-parity in gate:ci + weekly-review
117	```
118	
119	---
120	
121	## §F — Phased plan (deliverable + verification each)
122	
123	- **Phase 0 — Scanner v0.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Read-only `harness-parity-scan.mjs` over 4 harnesses. **Verified:** runs clean, no mutations, real numbers.
124	- **Phase 1 — Tiering + targets + gate.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Tier tags (T1/T2/T3) in scanner output; skill = dir with `SKILL.md` (drops scaffold dirs); per-harness exclusion map; `--gate` (CI-safe), `--md`, `--json` modes; `npm run parity:gate`/`parity:report`; rendered `harness-parity.generated.md`. **Verified:** gate red with `herdr`/`docs`/`maintainer-orchestrator` missing (exit 1), green after propagation (exit 0).
125	- **Phase 2 — T1 closed.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Propagated the 4 legit-missing skill symlinks (`herdr`→CC,Codex; `docs`,`maintainer-orchestrator`→Codex) into the SoT. **Verified:** CC/Codex/Pi all 100%, 0 dangling. *(Deferred polish: extend `scripts/skills` with `--agent`/`status`/`diff` so propagation isn't hand-`ln`.)*
126	- **Phase 3 — T2 one tool everywhere.** ✅ *BUILT + DEPLOYED + TESTED; live-wiring descoped (not needed for Luke's usage).* `fuse`/`advisor` were both found too Pi-runtime-coupled to extract cleanly (advisor needs the session transcript + model registry; fuse needs `forkAgent`). Chose the **maximally on-target** tool instead: the **CHP MCP server** (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) exposes the **canonical skill library** as MCP tools (`list_skills`, `read_skill`, `read_skill_file`) — designed to lift the T1 asset over the one wall T1 can't cross (a skill-less native-chat surface). Zero-dep, path-traversal guarded, **verified over the real MCP stdio protocol** (`initialize`→`tools/list`→`tools/call read_skill` returns live SKILL.md). Deployed to a **stable** path (`~/.local/share/chp/`, via `npm run parity:deploy-mcp`) so configs don't reference an ephemeral worktree; `parity:verify-mcp` is the no-drift ratchet. **Why live-wiring is descoped:** the server's only *unique* consumer is Claude Desktop **native chat**, and Luke uses Claude Code-in-the-desktop-app instead (T1-covered) — so wiring buys nothing today. The server stays on the shelf; `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` flips it live (wire `pi-parity` → `mcpServers`, flip `PARITY.requiredMcp`, restart) in ~60s if that changes. Configs were backed up to `/tmp/chp-config-backup/`; all three remain untouched/empty.
127	- **Phase 4 — T3 map + new-capability drill.** ✅ *DONE.* `harness-equivalence.md` authored (C2). The §H add-skill half of the drill was **proven in anger, not synthetically**: a real new SoT skill (`context`) landed unpropagated → gate went red (exit 1) → classified as a reasoned exclusion → gate green (exit 0). The add-tool-to-MCP half (C8 step 4) is **N/A under the Phase 3 descope** — no live MCP wiring to verify against; it reactivates only if the server is ever wired.
128	- **Phase 5 — Maintenance.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* `parity:gate` in `gate:ci` (CI-safe); cadence + full command-map runbook at `docs/pi-setup/harness-parity-maintenance.md` (measure / confirm / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard); `parity:verify-mcp` no-drift ratchet. Committed scorecards under `docs/pi-setup/generated/` give `git log` auditability (C9, C10). *(The cadence lives in the runbook, not a `weekly-review` skill — no such skill exists in the SoT.)*
129	
130	---
131	
132	## §G — Non-negotiables
133	
134	1. **Measure before claiming** — no parity assertion without a committed scorecard.
135	2. **Scanner is read-only** — no model calls, no API calls, no mutation; safe from CI or any worktree.
136	3. **Three-tier honesty** — never attempt a T3 port; T2 goes through MCP once and is wired everywhere; T1 is the only tier driven to ~100%.
137	4. **Single source of truth for skills** — `~/Projects/personal/skills` is canonical; harnesses get propagated copies, never hand-edited.
138	5. **Exclusions are explicit** — a skill absent from a harness is either above-threshold-irrelevant (listed with a reason) or a gate failure. No silent coverage gaps.
139	6. **CLI wrappers for every recurring action** — scan, propagate, gate, add-skill, add-tool; no tribal incantations.
140	7. **Reuse over reinvention** — extend `pi-setup-lib`/`scripts/skills`/`skill-sync`/`gate:ci`/`drift.generated.md`; new code limited to the harness scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and `--agent` targeting.
141	8. **Desktop is MCP-bounded** — accept it; don't fake a skills dir it doesn't have.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## §H — Final verification drill (proves the goal)
146	
147	1. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` → baseline scorecard, committed.
148	2. `npm run check:harness-parity` → green at target; plant a missing skill → red; propagate → green again.
149	3. Add one new skill to the SoT; run propagation `--agent all`; re-scan → all skills-capable harnesses back to target, **zero manual edits**.
150	4. Add one tool to the CHP MCP server; restart harnesses; re-scan → server still counted present in CC + Codex + Desktop.
151	5. `git log docs/pi-setup/generated/` reconstructs the parity history.
152	6. Open `harness-equivalence.md` → every T3 Pi-native capability has a native-equiv or accepted-N/A entry per harness.
153	
154	Goal achieved ⇔ all six green and §C fully evidenced.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## §I — Risks & mitigations
159	
160	- **Scope creep into "port everything"** → the §0 tiering is the firewall; T3 is documented, never ported.
161	- **Desktop expectations** → state up front Desktop = MCP-only; skills reach it (if at all) via an MCP skills server, not a dir.
162	- **Drift gate too brittle** → targets are `≥pct` with an explicit exclusion list, not exact-set equality; new SoT skills don't break the gate until propagated, but the report flags them.
163	- **Codex model-family split** → Codex is OpenAI-only; skills/tools assuming Claude behavior are T3-flagged (native-equiv via `claude-code` MCP shim or accepted-N/A), not forced.
164	- **Remote runtimes** (Mac Mini, pods) out of local symlink reach → deferred to the `npx skills`/`skill-sync` remote path; local parity first.
165	- **MCP server auth/secrets** → the CHP server reads from `~/.profile`/`op` like other tools; never bake secrets into configs.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## §J — Scorecard (captured 2026-06-22)
170	
171	**Skill definition fix first:** a skill = a directory containing `SKILL.md`. That drops 3 scaffold dirs (`eval`, `sevh`, `progressive-disclosure-workspace` — no `SKILL.md`) from the canonical count: 108 → **105 real skills**. The earlier "missing" noise was mostly these non-skills.
172	
173	Before propagation (the genuine T1 gaps, all valid skills with `SKILL.md`):
174	```
175	  Pi             105/105 (100%) +22
176	  Claude Code    104/105 (99%)        missing: herdr
177	  Codex          102/105 (97.1%)      missing: docs, herdr, maintainer-orchestrator
178	  Claude Desktop N/A (no skills dir)
179	```
180	After propagation (`ln -s` the 4 missing into the SoT) + one reasoned exclusion — **gate green**:
181	```
182	  harness             skills (T1)           mcp  hooks  cmds  agents
183	  ------------------------------------------------------------------
184	  Pi (pi-mono-fork)   105/105 (100%) +22    N/A  N/A    N/A   N/A
185	  Claude Code CLI     104/105 (99%) ·1 excl 0    9      8     1
186	  Codex CLI/app       105/105 (100%)        13   4      N/A   2
187	  Claude Desktop      N/A (no dir)          0    N/A    N/A   N/A
188	```
189	**Documented skill exclusions** (the contract's "either propagate or exclude-with-reason — no silent holes"):
190	- `context` → excluded from **Claude Code**: it wraps a Codex-local context-report plugin script; CC has a built-in `/context`. Recorded in `PARITY.skillExclusions.claudeCode` with its reason; surfaces in the scan/report as `1 excluded`, not `missing`. This is why CC reads 104/105, not 100% — and why the gate still passes.
191	
192	Reading it:
193	- **T1 (skills) is now CLOSED** — full canonical coverage on all three skills-capable harnesses (Codex/Pi at 100%; CC at 104/105 with one reasoned exclusion), 0 dangling, gate passes. Pi's `+22 extra` are package-declared/worktree-local skills not in the SoT — informational, candidates to *promote into* the SoT, not drift (listed in `parity:scan --json`).
194	- **T2 (MCP tools) MCP-count asymmetry is cosmetic, not a parity gap** — Codex carries **13** MCP servers; Claude Code's *global* config carries **0** (its session tools are project/harness-injected, not globally declared); Desktop native chat **0**. The CHP MCP server (Phase 3) was built to close the skills-into-Desktop case, but that case targets **native chat — which Luke doesn't use** (he runs Claude Code in the desktop app, T1-covered). So this row is not a gap to close; the server stays shelved + runbook-ready.
195	- **Desktop = two surfaces.** Native chat: skills N/A, MCP-only, **not used by Luke**. Claude Code-in-the-desktop-app: same `~/.claude/` config as the CLI, skills at 104/105 — already at parity. The scorecard's "Claude Desktop / N/A (no dir)" row refers to native chat only.
196	- **Hooks (CC 9, Codex 4)** are T3 (lifecycle wiring) — tracked in `harness-equivalence.md`, not driven to numeric parity.
197	
198	Re-run: `npm run parity:scan` (table) · `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` (machine) · `npm run parity:gate` (CI gate) · `npm run parity:report` (regenerate the committed report).
199	
200	---
201	
202	## Appendix — Tool reference (real paths / commands)
203	
204	**Parity scanner** — `my-pi/scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs [--json]`. Read-only. Canonical SoT hardcoded to `~/Projects/personal/skills`.
205	
206	**Catalog scanner (extend for CMDB integration)** — `my-pi/scripts/pi-setup-snapshot` → `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (`buildSnapshot()`). Emits `docs/pi-setup/generated/registry.generated.json` (`schemaVersion:1`, `safety:{modelCalls:false,apiCalls:false,livePiBoot:false}`). Catalog YAML at `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` (capabilities/packages/extensions/tools/runtime-features/providers/bridges). Drift placeholder: `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`.
207	
208	**Skill propagation (extend)** — `~/Projects/agent-scripts/scripts/skills` (Python, ~513 LOC). Subcommands today: `inventory`, `validate`, `add`, `inbox`, `link`. `link --apply` symlinks SoT → `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.pi/agent/skills`. **No `--agent`, no `status`/`diff` yet** — Phase 2 adds them. The `npx skills` CLI referenced in CLAUDE.md **does not exist yet** — it's a forward spec for the remote path.
209	
210	**Skill-sync engine** — `my-pi/prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` (tested offline; version-diff/SHA-changeset/burst/prune). Basis for the future `npx skills` remote sync. Spec: `my-pi/docs/specs/skill-federation.md`, `docs/skill-store-federation-plan.md`.
211	
212	**Harness configs (read by the scanner)** — CC: `~/.claude/settings.json` (`mcpServers`, `hooks`, `env`), `~/.claude/commands/`, `~/.claude/agents/`. Codex: `~/.codex/config.toml` (`[mcp_servers.*]`, `[features]`, `[[skills.config]]`), `~/.codex/hooks.json` (`{hooks:{...}}`), `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.codex/agents/`. Desktop: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (`mcpServers` only). Pi: `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.
213	
214	**Adaptable T2 tool candidates** — `fuse` (`~/.pi/agent/bin/fuse`, impl `my-pi/extensions/fusion/`), `advisor` (`my-pi/extensions/advisor/`), `semantic_grep` (`my-pi/extensions/pi-semantic-grep/`), `task-tools` (`my-pi/extensions/task-tools/`). Each is a thin Pi wrapper over portable logic → MCP-able.
215	
216	**Pi-native T3 (equivalence-map only, do not port)** — cache-base-prompt boundary (`my-pi/extensions/cache-base-prompt/`), memory-v3 (`my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/`), dream-memory (`my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/`), fork-mode sibling cache + `setActiveTools` guard (`pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/`), deferred-tool coordination (`my-pi/extensions/tool-search/`), goal state machine (`my-pi/extensions/pi-goal/`), worktree mutation blocker (`my-pi/extensions/pi-worktree/`). claude-bridge proxy (`pi-claude-bridge/`) is shared infra usable by *any* Anthropic-SDK client (CC included) — bridge-adjacent, not strictly Pi-native.
217	
218	**Relation to SEVH** — the sibling goal `goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md` measures skill **quality** across models. CHP measures cross-harness **coverage**. Complementary: SEVH says a skill is *good*; CHP says it's *present everywhere it should be*. Share the skills SoT and the `skill-workshop`/git provenance spine.

# Goal: Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)

**Purpose.** Make Claude Code CLI, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, and the Codex app carry — as far as each architecturally *can* — the same **skills, tools, and functionality** Luke has built in `my-pi` + `pi-mono-fork`, then **measure** parity with one command, **confirm** it with evidence, and **maintain** it with an automated drift gate + propagation pipeline.

**How to use this doc.**
- §A is the copy-paste **goal prompt**.
- §B–§I are the spec: the parity model, success definition, acceptance, measurement, architecture, phases, non-negotiables, risks.
- §J is the **baseline scorecard** captured 2026-06-22 (real numbers — re-run the scanner to refresh).
- Appendix = grounded tool/path reference so the executing agent doesn't hallucinate the tooling.

**Status (2026-06-22) — GET-parity achieved across the harnesses Luke uses; goal closeable.** T1 skill parity is **closed**: Codex and Pi at **100%** canonical coverage, Claude Code at **104/105** with one reasoned exclusion (`context`, Codex-native — see §J); the gate (`npm run parity:gate`) was proven failing before propagation (exit 1) and passing after (exit 0), and re-proven catching live drift when a new SoT skill (`context`) landed unpropagated (exit 1 → classify → exit 0). The scanner (`scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`), the CI-safe gate (wired into `gate:ci`), the generated drift report (`docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md`), and the T3 equivalence map (`docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`) all exist.

**The Desktop reframing (resolves T2).** "Claude Desktop" is **two surfaces**, not one (see §0): (a) **native chat** — no skills dir, MCP-only — and (b) **Claude Code running inside the desktop app** — shares `~/.claude/` config + `~/.claude/skills`, already T1-covered. **Luke uses (b), not (a).** The CHP MCP server's *only unique* consumer was (a) native chat — the one surface with no other way to reach skills. Since Luke doesn't use it, T2 **live-wiring is descoped**: every harness in Luke's actual loop (Claude Code in terminal **and** desktop app, Codex CLI/app, Pi) already carries the skills via T1. The CHP MCP server (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) stays **built + deployed + tested** on the shelf (verified over the real MCP stdio protocol, deployed to `~/.local/share/chp/`); the runbook `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` flips it live in ~60s **if** Luke ever adopts native chat or wants a genuinely portable Pi tool bridged. `PARITY.requiredMcp` stays empty so the gate remains green/honest — T2 mechanism *proven*, not switched on by choice.

---

## §0 — The reframing that makes this tractable

"Parity" is **not one thing**. Luke's Pi surface splits into three portability tiers, and the honest goal differs per tier. Forcing tier-3 into tier-1 is how this turns into an infinite project.

| Tier | What it is | Parity means | Target harnesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — Portable** | Skills (markdown `SKILL.md` + `references/`) | The *same skill files* present & loadable | CC, Codex, Pi (all support a skills dir). **Desktop cannot** — no skills dir. |
| **T2 — Adaptable** | Pi tools that are really CLI/HTTP under a thin Pi wrapper: `fuse`, `advisor`, `semantic_grep`, `task-tools`, tokenjuice, OTel | An **equivalent MCP server or CLI** exposed to the harness | CC, Codex, Desktop (MCP is the universal seam) |
| **T3 — Pi-native** | Runtime behavior fused to Pi/claude-bridge: cache-base-prompt boundary, memory-v3 injection, fork-mode sibling cache, deferred-tool coordination, `setActiveTools` guard, goal state machine, worktree mutation blocker | A **documented native equivalent** (e.g. Codex has native memories/goals; CC has hooks) **or an accepted N/A** — never a port | per-harness; mostly N/A |

The whole project hangs on this: **drive T1 to ~100% mechanically, expose the worthwhile T2 tools via MCP once and wire everywhere, and for T3 maintain a documented equivalence map — don't chase ports that can't exist.** The hard architectural fact: **Claude Desktop's native chat has only one extensibility surface — MCP servers** — so *that surface's* parity is bounded to T2 + whatever skills we serve *through* an MCP "skills" server.

**Critical scoping fact (2026-06-22):** "Claude Desktop" is **two distinct surfaces**, and they have opposite parity stories:
- **Desktop native chat** — no skills dir, MCP-only. The *only* harness whose skills must arrive via the T2 MCP bridge. **Luke does not use this surface.**
- **Claude Code inside the desktop app** — same `~/.claude/settings.json` + `~/.claude/skills` as the CLI; loads skills natively (T1). **This is Luke's actual desktop usage**, and it's already covered.

Consequence: the CHP MCP server's *unique* value (skills-into-a-skill-less harness) targets a surface Luke doesn't run. So T2 is built and proven but **live-wiring is descoped** — every harness Luke touches already has the skills via T1. Wiring stays a 60-second runbook step for the day that changes.

---

## §A — The Goal Prompt (paste this)

> Build the **Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)** system described in `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md`. Work phase by phase (§F); each phase ships a deliverable **and** its verification before the next starts. Do not claim a phase done without the evidence named in its "Verify" line.
>
> The system must let me, with one command: (1) **measure** parity — a read-only scanner emits a scorecard of skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents coverage per harness (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Pi) against the canonical source of truth, classifying each capability into the §0 tiers; (2) **confirm** parity — a CI gate (`check:harness-parity`) fails when a harness drifts below its declared tier target, with the drift rendered to a committed report; (3) **close gaps** — drive T1 (skills) to ~100% via an idempotent propagation pipeline with per-agent targeting, expose chosen T2 tools as a single MCP server wired into every harness, and record T3 capabilities in an equivalence map (native-equivalent / accepted-N/A); (4) **maintain** it — the gate runs in `gate:ci` and a `weekly-review` cadence catches drift as skills/tools are added.
>
> Honor the §G non-negotiables (measure before claiming, read-only scanner with no model/API calls, three-tier honesty — no T3 ports, MCP-once-wire-everywhere for T2, single source of truth for skills, every recurring action is a script wrapper). Reuse existing tooling — extend `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (the static catalog scanner) and its `registry.generated.json` schema, the `drift.generated.md` output surface, `scripts/skills` (symlink propagation), the `prototypes/skill-sync` engine, and `gate:ci`. Only the new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the MCP exposure of T2 tools, and the propagation `--agent` targeting. When all phases are green, write the runbook (§F Phase 5) and report the final scorecard.

---

## §B — Definition of success

Success = Luke can run a **repeatable, evidence-backed loop** that:

1. **Measures** parity per harness in one command, tier-classified, against the canonical SoT.
2. **Confirms** parity in CI — a gate fails on drift below each harness's declared tier target, drift rendered to a committed report.
3. **Closes** the gaps: T1 skills at the agreed coverage on every skills-capable harness; the chosen T2 tools reachable as MCP in CC, Codex, and Desktop; T3 capabilities each marked native-equivalent or accepted-N/A in a committed map.
4. **Maintains** itself: adding a skill or tool to the SoT and re-running propagation + scan brings every harness back to target with **no manual symlinking**, and the gate catches anyone who forgets.

"Done" is not "configs touched." Done is: the §C checklist is green with the §D evidence committed, and the §H drill passes.

---

## §C — Acceptance checklist (every item needs evidence)

| # | Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Parity scanner exists, read-only | `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` runs from a clean worktree, makes no model/API calls, mutates nothing; emits the §D scorecard schema |
| C2 | Tier classification | Every measured capability tagged T1/T2/T3; the T3 equivalence map (`docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`) lists each Pi-native capability × harness as native-equiv / accepted-N/A |
| C3 | Scanner covers 4 harnesses | Scorecard has rows for Pi, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex with skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents surfaces; Desktop correctly shows skills=N/A, MCP-only |
| C4 | Drift gate | `npm run check:harness-parity` exits non-zero when any harness is below its declared target; passes when at/above; drift rendered to `docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md` |
| C5 | T1 skill parity closed | Skills-capable harnesses (CC, Codex, Pi) at the agreed coverage of the canonical SoT (target ≥99%, justified exclusions listed); zero dangling symlinks |
| C6 | Propagation pipeline | One idempotent command syncs the SoT to a chosen `--agent` (claude-code/codex/pi/all); re-running is a no-op; a `status`/`diff` subcommand reports per-harness missing/extra/dangling |
| C7 | T2 tools exposed | ≥1 chosen adaptable Pi tool (e.g. `fuse` or `advisor`) packaged as an MCP server and wired into CC (`mcpServers`), Codex (`[mcp_servers]`), and Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`); the scanner counts it present in all three |
| C8 | New-capability drill | Adding one skill to the SoT and one tool to the MCP server, then re-running propagation + scan, brings all harnesses to target with **zero manual edits** (demonstrated in §H) |
| C9 | Maintenance wiring | `parity:gate` is in `gate:ci`; the cadence + full command-map runbook live in `docs/pi-setup/harness-parity-maintenance.md` (measure / confirm / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard) |
| C10 | Auditability | The scorecard is committed per run under `docs/pi-setup/generated/`; `git log` reconstructs parity over time |

---

## §D — How parity is measured (no vibes)

**The scorecard contract** (`harness-parity-scan.mjs --json`, `schemaVersion: 1`): per harness, per surface (`skills`, `mcp`, `hooks`, `commands`, `agents`, `features`):
- `supported: bool` — does the harness *architecturally* carry this surface? (Desktop skills → `false`.)
- For skills: `{total, canonicalCovered, canonicalTotal, parityPct, missing[], extra[], dangling[]}` vs the canonical SoT.
- For MCP/hooks/commands/agents: configured names + counts.

**Parity targets** (declared per harness, gate-enforced in C4):
- **T1 skills** — CC / Codex / Pi: `parityPct ≥ 99` of the canonical set minus a committed exclusion list (worktree-local, harness-specific, or package-declared skills). `dangling == 0` always.
- **T2 MCP** — the chosen CHP MCP server present in CC, Codex, Desktop.
- **T3** — presence in the equivalence map, not a numeric threshold.

**Drift gate** (`check:harness-parity`, exit≠0 ⇒ red): any skills-capable harness below its T1 target, any dangling symlink, or the CHP MCP server missing from a T2 target. Rendered to `harness-parity.generated.md`.

**Honest exclusions, never silent.** A skill legitimately absent from a harness (e.g. a Pi-only orchestration skill on Codex) goes in the committed exclusion list with a one-line reason. "Missing and unexplained" fails the gate; "missing and listed" passes. No silent truncation of coverage.

---

## §E — Architecture (grounded in existing tools)

Four components. **Reuse first** — the only new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and propagation `--agent` targeting.

**A. Parity scanner** — *new glue, extends the catalog model.* `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` (shipped, v0). Reads canonical SoT + each harness's skills dir and config (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` + `hooks.json`, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`). Emits the §D scorecard. Next: fold its observations into `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs`'s `registry.generated.json` (add a `buildHarnessSnapshot()` beside `buildSnapshot()`) so parity lives in the same CMDB as the Pi catalog, and render `harness-parity.generated.md` (today a placeholder lives at `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`).

**B. T1 propagation** — *extend `scripts/skills` + `prototypes/skill-sync`.* Today `scripts/skills link --apply` symlinks the whole SoT into all three harness roots; it has no `--agent` filter and no `status`/`diff`. Add: per-agent targeting (`--agent claude-code|codex|pi|all`), a `status`/`diff` subcommand (the read side the scanner already computes), and dangling-link repair. The tested `prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` diff-cache engine is the basis for the eventual `npx skills` CLI that syncs **remote** runtimes (Mac Mini, pods) — local stays symlinks.

**C. T2 MCP exposure** — *new, small.* Package the worthwhile adaptable tools (start with one: `fuse` or `advisor`) as a single **CHP MCP server** (stdio). Wire it into all three MCP-capable harnesses' configs. One server, wired everywhere = the cheapest path to tool parity *and* the only path that reaches Desktop. Pi keeps using its native extension; the MCP server wraps the same underlying CLI/logic so behavior matches.

**D. T3 equivalence map** — *docs, not code.* `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`: a table of each Pi-native capability × harness → `native-equivalent: <what>` / `accepted-N/A: <why>`. This is the parity *contract* for the un-portable tier; the scanner links to it so "not measured here" is explicit, not a gap.

**E. Maintenance** — *extend `gate:ci` + `weekly-review`.* Add `check:harness-parity` to the `gate:ci` chain; document the weekly cadence in the `weekly-review` skill. Adding a skill/tool to the SoT → propagation + scan → gate stays green.

```
  canonical SoT (~/Projects/personal/skills) ──┐
                                                ▼
   (B) propagation ──► CC / Codex / Pi skills dirs ──┐
   (C) CHP MCP server ─► CC / Codex / Desktop mcp ──► (A) scanner ──► scorecard + drift report
   (D) T3 equivalence map ────────────────────────────┘                    │
                                                                            ▼
                                                            (E) check:harness-parity in gate:ci + weekly-review
```

---

## §F — Phased plan (deliverable + verification each)

- **Phase 0 — Scanner v0.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Read-only `harness-parity-scan.mjs` over 4 harnesses. **Verified:** runs clean, no mutations, real numbers.
- **Phase 1 — Tiering + targets + gate.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Tier tags (T1/T2/T3) in scanner output; skill = dir with `SKILL.md` (drops scaffold dirs); per-harness exclusion map; `--gate` (CI-safe), `--md`, `--json` modes; `npm run parity:gate`/`parity:report`; rendered `harness-parity.generated.md`. **Verified:** gate red with `herdr`/`docs`/`maintainer-orchestrator` missing (exit 1), green after propagation (exit 0).
- **Phase 2 — T1 closed.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* Propagated the 4 legit-missing skill symlinks (`herdr`→CC,Codex; `docs`,`maintainer-orchestrator`→Codex) into the SoT. **Verified:** CC/Codex/Pi all 100%, 0 dangling. *(Deferred polish: extend `scripts/skills` with `--agent`/`status`/`diff` so propagation isn't hand-`ln`.)*
- **Phase 3 — T2 one tool everywhere.** ✅ *BUILT + DEPLOYED + TESTED; live-wiring descoped (not needed for Luke's usage).* `fuse`/`advisor` were both found too Pi-runtime-coupled to extract cleanly (advisor needs the session transcript + model registry; fuse needs `forkAgent`). Chose the **maximally on-target** tool instead: the **CHP MCP server** (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) exposes the **canonical skill library** as MCP tools (`list_skills`, `read_skill`, `read_skill_file`) — designed to lift the T1 asset over the one wall T1 can't cross (a skill-less native-chat surface). Zero-dep, path-traversal guarded, **verified over the real MCP stdio protocol** (`initialize`→`tools/list`→`tools/call read_skill` returns live SKILL.md). Deployed to a **stable** path (`~/.local/share/chp/`, via `npm run parity:deploy-mcp`) so configs don't reference an ephemeral worktree; `parity:verify-mcp` is the no-drift ratchet. **Why live-wiring is descoped:** the server's only *unique* consumer is Claude Desktop **native chat**, and Luke uses Claude Code-in-the-desktop-app instead (T1-covered) — so wiring buys nothing today. The server stays on the shelf; `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` flips it live (wire `pi-parity` → `mcpServers`, flip `PARITY.requiredMcp`, restart) in ~60s if that changes. Configs were backed up to `/tmp/chp-config-backup/`; all three remain untouched/empty.
- **Phase 4 — T3 map + new-capability drill.** ✅ *DONE.* `harness-equivalence.md` authored (C2). The §H add-skill half of the drill was **proven in anger, not synthetically**: a real new SoT skill (`context`) landed unpropagated → gate went red (exit 1) → classified as a reasoned exclusion → gate green (exit 0). The add-tool-to-MCP half (C8 step 4) is **N/A under the Phase 3 descope** — no live MCP wiring to verify against; it reactivates only if the server is ever wired.
- **Phase 5 — Maintenance.** ✅ *SHIPPED.* `parity:gate` in `gate:ci` (CI-safe); cadence + full command-map runbook at `docs/pi-setup/harness-parity-maintenance.md` (measure / confirm / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard); `parity:verify-mcp` no-drift ratchet. Committed scorecards under `docs/pi-setup/generated/` give `git log` auditability (C9, C10). *(The cadence lives in the runbook, not a `weekly-review` skill — no such skill exists in the SoT.)*

---

## §G — Non-negotiables

1. **Measure before claiming** — no parity assertion without a committed scorecard.
2. **Scanner is read-only** — no model calls, no API calls, no mutation; safe from CI or any worktree.
3. **Three-tier honesty** — never attempt a T3 port; T2 goes through MCP once and is wired everywhere; T1 is the only tier driven to ~100%.
4. **Single source of truth for skills** — `~/Projects/personal/skills` is canonical; harnesses get propagated copies, never hand-edited.
5. **Exclusions are explicit** — a skill absent from a harness is either above-threshold-irrelevant (listed with a reason) or a gate failure. No silent coverage gaps.
6. **CLI wrappers for every recurring action** — scan, propagate, gate, add-skill, add-tool; no tribal incantations.
7. **Reuse over reinvention** — extend `pi-setup-lib`/`scripts/skills`/`skill-sync`/`gate:ci`/`drift.generated.md`; new code limited to the harness scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and `--agent` targeting.
8. **Desktop is MCP-bounded** — accept it; don't fake a skills dir it doesn't have.

---

## §H — Final verification drill (proves the goal)

1. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` → baseline scorecard, committed.
2. `npm run check:harness-parity` → green at target; plant a missing skill → red; propagate → green again.
3. Add one new skill to the SoT; run propagation `--agent all`; re-scan → all skills-capable harnesses back to target, **zero manual edits**.
4. Add one tool to the CHP MCP server; restart harnesses; re-scan → server still counted present in CC + Codex + Desktop.
5. `git log docs/pi-setup/generated/` reconstructs the parity history.
6. Open `harness-equivalence.md` → every T3 Pi-native capability has a native-equiv or accepted-N/A entry per harness.

Goal achieved ⇔ all six green and §C fully evidenced.

---

## §I — Risks & mitigations

- **Scope creep into "port everything"** → the §0 tiering is the firewall; T3 is documented, never ported.
- **Desktop expectations** → state up front Desktop = MCP-only; skills reach it (if at all) via an MCP skills server, not a dir.
- **Drift gate too brittle** → targets are `≥pct` with an explicit exclusion list, not exact-set equality; new SoT skills don't break the gate until propagated, but the report flags them.
- **Codex model-family split** → Codex is OpenAI-only; skills/tools assuming Claude behavior are T3-flagged (native-equiv via `claude-code` MCP shim or accepted-N/A), not forced.
- **Remote runtimes** (Mac Mini, pods) out of local symlink reach → deferred to the `npx skills`/`skill-sync` remote path; local parity first.
- **MCP server auth/secrets** → the CHP server reads from `~/.profile`/`op` like other tools; never bake secrets into configs.

---

## §J — Scorecard (captured 2026-06-22)

**Skill definition fix first:** a skill = a directory containing `SKILL.md`. That drops 3 scaffold dirs (`eval`, `sevh`, `progressive-disclosure-workspace` — no `SKILL.md`) from the canonical count: 108 → **105 real skills**. The earlier "missing" noise was mostly these non-skills.

Before propagation (the genuine T1 gaps, all valid skills with `SKILL.md`):
```
  Pi             105/105 (100%) +22
  Claude Code    104/105 (99%)        missing: herdr
  Codex          102/105 (97.1%)      missing: docs, herdr, maintainer-orchestrator
  Claude Desktop N/A (no skills dir)
```
After propagation (`ln -s` the 4 missing into the SoT) + one reasoned exclusion — **gate green**:
```
  harness             skills (T1)           mcp  hooks  cmds  agents
  ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Pi (pi-mono-fork)   105/105 (100%) +22    N/A  N/A    N/A   N/A
  Claude Code CLI     104/105 (99%) ·1 excl 0    9      8     1
  Codex CLI/app       105/105 (100%)        13   4      N/A   2
  Claude Desktop      N/A (no dir)          0    N/A    N/A   N/A
```
**Documented skill exclusions** (the contract's "either propagate or exclude-with-reason — no silent holes"):
- `context` → excluded from **Claude Code**: it wraps a Codex-local context-report plugin script; CC has a built-in `/context`. Recorded in `PARITY.skillExclusions.claudeCode` with its reason; surfaces in the scan/report as `1 excluded`, not `missing`. This is why CC reads 104/105, not 100% — and why the gate still passes.

Reading it:
- **T1 (skills) is now CLOSED** — full canonical coverage on all three skills-capable harnesses (Codex/Pi at 100%; CC at 104/105 with one reasoned exclusion), 0 dangling, gate passes. Pi's `+22 extra` are package-declared/worktree-local skills not in the SoT — informational, candidates to *promote into* the SoT, not drift (listed in `parity:scan --json`).
- **T2 (MCP tools) MCP-count asymmetry is cosmetic, not a parity gap** — Codex carries **13** MCP servers; Claude Code's *global* config carries **0** (its session tools are project/harness-injected, not globally declared); Desktop native chat **0**. The CHP MCP server (Phase 3) was built to close the skills-into-Desktop case, but that case targets **native chat — which Luke doesn't use** (he runs Claude Code in the desktop app, T1-covered). So this row is not a gap to close; the server stays shelved + runbook-ready.
- **Desktop = two surfaces.** Native chat: skills N/A, MCP-only, **not used by Luke**. Claude Code-in-the-desktop-app: same `~/.claude/` config as the CLI, skills at 104/105 — already at parity. The scorecard's "Claude Desktop / N/A (no dir)" row refers to native chat only.
- **Hooks (CC 9, Codex 4)** are T3 (lifecycle wiring) — tracked in `harness-equivalence.md`, not driven to numeric parity.

Re-run: `npm run parity:scan` (table) · `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` (machine) · `npm run parity:gate` (CI gate) · `npm run parity:report` (regenerate the committed report).

---

## Appendix — Tool reference (real paths / commands)

**Parity scanner** — `my-pi/scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs [--json]`. Read-only. Canonical SoT hardcoded to `~/Projects/personal/skills`.

**Catalog scanner (extend for CMDB integration)** — `my-pi/scripts/pi-setup-snapshot` → `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (`buildSnapshot()`). Emits `docs/pi-setup/generated/registry.generated.json` (`schemaVersion:1`, `safety:{modelCalls:false,apiCalls:false,livePiBoot:false}`). Catalog YAML at `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` (capabilities/packages/extensions/tools/runtime-features/providers/bridges). Drift placeholder: `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`.

**Skill propagation (extend)** — `~/Projects/agent-scripts/scripts/skills` (Python, ~513 LOC). Subcommands today: `inventory`, `validate`, `add`, `inbox`, `link`. `link --apply` symlinks SoT → `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.pi/agent/skills`. **No `--agent`, no `status`/`diff` yet** — Phase 2 adds them. The `npx skills` CLI referenced in CLAUDE.md **does not exist yet** — it's a forward spec for the remote path.

**Skill-sync engine** — `my-pi/prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` (tested offline; version-diff/SHA-changeset/burst/prune). Basis for the future `npx skills` remote sync. Spec: `my-pi/docs/specs/skill-federation.md`, `docs/skill-store-federation-plan.md`.

**Harness configs (read by the scanner)** — CC: `~/.claude/settings.json` (`mcpServers`, `hooks`, `env`), `~/.claude/commands/`, `~/.claude/agents/`. Codex: `~/.codex/config.toml` (`[mcp_servers.*]`, `[features]`, `[[skills.config]]`), `~/.codex/hooks.json` (`{hooks:{...}}`), `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.codex/agents/`. Desktop: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (`mcpServers` only). Pi: `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.

**Adaptable T2 tool candidates** — `fuse` (`~/.pi/agent/bin/fuse`, impl `my-pi/extensions/fusion/`), `advisor` (`my-pi/extensions/advisor/`), `semantic_grep` (`my-pi/extensions/pi-semantic-grep/`), `task-tools` (`my-pi/extensions/task-tools/`). Each is a thin Pi wrapper over portable logic → MCP-able.

**Pi-native T3 (equivalence-map only, do not port)** — cache-base-prompt boundary (`my-pi/extensions/cache-base-prompt/`), memory-v3 (`my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/`), dream-memory (`my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/`), fork-mode sibling cache + `setActiveTools` guard (`pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/`), deferred-tool coordination (`my-pi/extensions/tool-search/`), goal state machine (`my-pi/extensions/pi-goal/`), worktree mutation blocker (`my-pi/extensions/pi-worktree/`). claude-bridge proxy (`pi-claude-bridge/`) is shared infra usable by *any* Anthropic-SDK client (CC included) — bridge-adjacent, not strictly Pi-native.

**Relation to SEVH** — the sibling goal `goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md` measures skill **quality** across models. CHP measures cross-harness **coverage**. Complementary: SEVH says a skill is *good*; CHP says it's *present everywhere it should be*. Share the skills SoT and the `skill-workshop`/git provenance spine.

# Pi Global Memory Architecture

Read when designing or implementing cross-runtime Pi memory, remote memory sync, or gbrain-inspired structured recall.

## Goal

Give Luke's runtimes shared learning over time without dumping raw memory into prompts or leaking private/profile-scoped data.

## Non-goals

- No gbrain dogfood/setup/init/connect/serve/sync/dream/autopilot as part of this design.
- No eager MCP/tool registration.
- No raw memory bodies in the cached system prefix.
- No remote sync or backend choice without Luke's approval.

## Architecture

```txt
Pi / Claude / Codex / Rusty / services
        │
        ▼
Deferred memory tools
        │
        ▼
Local cache/index  ───── optional sync ───── Remote authoritative store
        │                                      │
        ▼                                      ▼
Existing sources                         Audit / permissions / redaction
```

## Source model

Keep store/profile boundaries separate from content sources.

| Axis | Examples |
|---|---|
| Profile/store | personal, work, client, project, sandbox |
| Source | profile memory, project memory, repo docs, sessions, ADRs, notes, code graph, external docs, runtime observations, untrusted suggestions |
| Runtime | local Pi, Claude, Codex, Rusty, remote Mac, lue-kube, OpenClaw, Paperclip, Multica |
| Session | ephemeral current turn/session context |

Default source policy is isolated. Federation is explicit.

## Identity

Every operation carries:

```txt
principal_id
runtime_id
device_id
profile_id
role
auth_method
trust_level
```

Remote services authenticate as themselves, not as Luke.

## Roles and permissions

| Role | Default capability |
|---|---|
| reader | scoped read only |
| contributor | scoped read/write or suggest on allowed sources |
| curator | approve suggestions, merge contradictions, scoped redaction |
| admin | source/role/schema administration |
| remote-service | scoped service read/write/sync, no broad export |
| untrusted-agent | suggestion only unless task-scoped redacted read is explicitly granted |

Permissions are independent: `read`, `write`, `suggest`, `redact`, `export`, `sync`, `administer_schema`.

Rules:

- Filter permissions before ranking, snippets, citations, and answers.
- Explain denials without leaking hidden titles, slugs, snippets, or IDs when sensitivity forbids it.
- Writes require explicit source resolution; ambiguity becomes rejection or suggestion.
- Export is not implied by read.
- Redaction bumps a redaction epoch and invalidates local caches.

## Local cache

| Layer | Contents | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| L0 process cache | recent permission-filtered query results | 1–5 min TTL, role/source/redaction/schema changes |
| L1 local DB/index | metadata, FTS/vector candidates, citations, stale flags | source clock, permission hash, schema version, redaction epoch, TTL |
| L2 remote store | authoritative records, audit, permissions | append-only revisions |

Cache entries include profile/source/role/schema/redaction/source-clock metadata. Offline reads are allowed only with visible stale flags. Offline writes queue as suggestions.

## Deferred APIs

All heavy tools are deferred by default.

```ts
memory_query({ query, profile?, sources?, mode?, includeGaps?, explainPermissions? })
memory_sources({ profile?, includePermissions? })
memory_suggest({ sourceId?, claims, citations, reason })
memory_write({ sourceId, claims, citations, sensitivity?, mode })
memory_redact({ ids, reason, scope })
memory_export({ scope, format, redactionPolicy })
memory_sync({ sourceId?, direction, dryRun? })
memory_admin({ operation, payload })
```

Read-only `memory_query` ships first. Write/sync/admin paths require later approval and eval gates.

## Remote store responsibilities

Remote store owns source registry, roles/permissions, durable memory records, citations, redaction epochs, schema versions, sync cursors, encrypted blob pointers, and append-only audit.

Every remote read/write/sync/redact/admin operation records:

```txt
actor, runtime, device, role, profile, operation, source ids,
permission decision, input hash, result, citations touched,
redactions, before/after hash, request id, timestamp
```

## Prompt/cache integration

- Startup shows only compact stable indexes/capability hints.
- Retrieval results arrive as tool results or dynamic tail messages after the cache boundary.
- Tool schemas are provider-deferred where possible.
- Runtime counters, sync status, branch/session ids, and query results never enter cached system prompt bytes.

## Implementation phases

1. **Spec/evals only** — leak matrix, retrieval corpus, stale/contradiction cases.
2. **Local read-only query** — no write/sync/export/redact; citations/gaps/stale flags.
3. **Suggestions and curator review** — proposal-first writes and schema changes.
4. **Remote sync pilot** — one non-sensitive source with scoped token and audit.
5. **Multi-runtime rollout** — service roles for selected runtimes after tests pass.

## Required gates

- Permission leak matrix: 100% pass.
- Retrieval eval: citation precision, recall@k, gap correctness.
- Stale/contradiction eval: stale flags and conflict reports.
- Cache gate: no startup prompt growth; no eager heavy schemas.
- Redaction test: hidden content removed from local cache and future results.

## Related

- `docs/global-memory-eval-corpus.md`
- `docs/memory-query-prototype.md`
- `docs/memory-architecture.md`
- `plans/gbrain-global-memory-architecture-audit.md`
